title: Choplifter!
label: Brøderbund
description: Choplifter is a classic video game developed by Dan Gorlin and published by Ariolasoft in 1982. It's a side-scrolling shoot 'em up where players control a helicopter rescuing prisoners of war. With its innovative gameplay and challenging levels, "Choplifter" became a hit, showcasing Ariolasoft's commitment to quality and innovation in gaming during the early '80s.

title: David's Midnight Magic
label: Brøderbund
description:
David's Midnight Magic is an early home-computer pinball simulation created by David Snider. Brøderbund first published the Apple II original in 1982, followed by Atari 8-bit and Commodore 64 versions; Martin Kahn programmed the Commodore 64 conversion. Ariolasoft published the Commodore 64 edition in the UK and Europe.

The single-screen table was closely inspired by Williams' Black Knight machine. It recreates features unusual in early computer pinball, including Magna-Save, bonus multipliers, captured balls and multiball play. Up to four players can compete in turn.

The game was highly regarded at release and won Computer Game of the Year at the 1983 Arkie Awards. Its combination of responsive ball physics and recognisable mechanical-table features helped establish it as one of the important early home pinball simulations.
sources: Sources reviewed: MobyGames release record; David's Midnight Magic game documentation; contemporary Arkie Awards reporting.

title: Lode Runner
label: Brøderbund
description: Lode Runner is a classic puzzle-platform video game developed by Douglas E. Smith and released in 1983. Players control a character who must collect all the gold in a level while avoiding enemies and using strategically placed ladders and platforms. Known for its innovative gameplay and level editor, Lode Runner has become an iconic title in the history of video games.

title: Spelunker
label: Brøderbund
description: Spelunker is a classic platform video game originally released in 1983. Developed by Tim Martin and MicroGraphicImage, Spelunker challenges players to explore caves, avoid traps, and collect treasures. With its challenging gameplay and atmospheric music, Spelunker has become an iconic title in the history of video games, inspiring numerous sequels and remakes.

title: Axis Assassin
label: Electronic Arts
description: Axis Assassin is a video game developed and published by Electronic Arts in 1983. In the game, players control a covert operative infiltrating enemy territory to sabotage key installations. With its challenging gameplay and engaging storyline, Axis Assassin became a popular title among gamers during the early '80s.

title: Hard Hat Mack
label: Electronic Arts
description: Hard Hat Mack is a platformer video game developed and published by Electronic Arts in 1983. Players control a construction worker named Mack who must navigate through hazardous construction sites to complete tasks. Known for its challenging gameplay and colorful graphics, Hard Hat Mack garnered positive reviews from players and critics alike.

title: Operation Whirlwind
label: Brøderbund
description:
Operation Whirlwind is a Second World War strategy game created by Roger Damon and released by Brøderbund in 1983, with Ariolasoft publishing the European editions. The player commands an armoured battalion whose primary objective lies fifteen kilometres away across two rivers: take the city and hold it.

Terrain, obstacles and a capable enemy stand between the battalion and its objective. Victory requires seizing the city on schedule and then surviving the counterattack; failure leaves the front vulnerable to collapse. The game provides four difficulty levels, a realistic battlefield map, sound effects and on-screen status reports, while the disk edition can save a battle in progress.
sources: Original Ariolasoft back-cover description; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Whirlwind_(video_game)

title: Pinball Construction Set
label: Electronic Arts
description:
Pinball Construction Set was designed and programmed by Bill Budge, first published by BudgeCo for the Apple II in 1982 and released by Electronic Arts in 1983 with Atari 8-bit and Commodore 64 editions. Ariolasoft published the game in Europe.

Rather than supplying only a fixed table, it lets players construct their own pinball machines through a graphical drag-and-drop interface. Bumpers, flippers, spinners and other parts can be positioned freely, while gravity and aspects of the physics can be adjusted. Completed tables can be saved and shared, and can be played without the construction program.

The game established the construction-set genre and became one of the most influential early examples of user-generated game content.
sources: Source reviewed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinball_Construction_Set

title: D-Bug
label: Electronic Arts
description:
D-Bug is an educational action-strategy game developed by ChildWare Corporation and published by Electronic Arts in 1983 for the Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit computers. Ariolasoft subsequently released both versions in Europe.

The game begins with a two-player contest called Gotcha! before the computer running it breaks down. Charlie Fix-It, who lives inside the machine, must locate the fault and repair the bug. The result is a game within a game that introduces the components and failure modes of a home computer through a series of diagnostic challenges.
sources: Ariolasoft Autumn/Winter 1985 catalogue; MobyGames D-Bug release record; contemporary Electronic Arts material.

title: Music Construction Set
label: Electronic Arts
description:
Will Harvey's Music Construction Set turns musical notation into an approachable graphical construction kit. Notes are selected and placed directly onto a staff, after which the computer can play the composition back. Speed, volume, sound quality and key can be adjusted, while finished music can be printed. Built-in tunes, icon-driven commands and joystick control were intended to make it accessible to newcomers without limiting more serious experimentation.

Ariolasoft's 1985 catalogue offered the original, non-Deluxe program for Commodore 64/128, Atari 8-bit, Apple II and IBM PC/PCjr. Deluxe Music Construction Set was a later redesign for Amiga and Macintosh and is not included as this catalogue entry.
sources: Ariolasoft Autumn/Winter 1985 catalogue; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Construction_Set

title: M.U.L.E.
label: Electronic Arts
description: M.U.L.E. is a multiplayer economic simulation game developed by Ozark Softscape and published by Electronic Arts in 1983. Players compete to develop a colony on an alien planet by managing resources, trading goods, and outsmarting opponents. Renowned for its strategic depth and innovative gameplay, M.U.L.E. remains a classic in the realm of simulation games.

title: One-on-One
label: Electronic Arts
description: One-On-One is a basketball simulation video game developed and published by Electronic Arts in 1983. Featuring a one-on-one basketball match between Larry Bird and Julius Erving, players can experience intense basketball action on their computer screens. With its realistic gameplay and smooth controls, One-On-One became a favorite among sports gaming enthusiasts.

title: Kaiser
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Kaiser is a strategy video game developed by Ariolasoft and published by Ariolasoft in 1984. Set in the medieval era, players take on the role of a ruler striving to build and expand their empire. With its intricate mechanics and depth of gameplay, Kaiser offers a challenging yet rewarding experience for strategy enthusiasts.

            The game features various aspects of ruling, including managing resources, diplomacy, and military conquests. Players must make strategic decisions to balance their economy, maintain diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms, and lead their armies to victory on the battlefield. With its detailed simulation of medieval governance and warfare, Kaiser stands out as a classic in the genre of strategy games.

title: Valkyrie 17
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Valkyrie 17 is a sci-fi action-adventure game developed by Ram Jam and published by Ariolasoft in 1984. Set in a dystopian future, players assume the role of a rebel fighter on a mission to overthrow a tyrannical regime. With its immersive storyline and captivating gameplay, Valkyrie 17 offers an unforgettable gaming experience.

            The game features a mix of platforming, puzzle-solving, and combat elements, as players navigate through futuristic environments, uncovering secrets and battling enemies along the way. With its cutting-edge graphics and innovative gameplay mechanics, Valkyrie 17 pushed the boundaries of what was possible in gaming at the time, earning critical acclaim and a dedicated fanbase.

title: Wizard
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Wizard is a fantasy role-playing game developed by Progressive and published by Ariolasoft in 1984. Set in a magical world filled with mythical creatures and ancient mysteries, players embark on a quest to defeat the evil sorcerer and save the realm. With its immersive storytelling and expansive world, Wizard offers an unparalleled gaming experience.

            Players assume the role of a young wizard-in-training, tasked with mastering powerful spells, exploring dangerous dungeons, and recruiting allies to aid in their quest. With its open-ended gameplay and non-linear progression, Wizard provides players with the freedom to explore the world at their own pace and forge their own path to victory.

title: Karateka
label: Brøderbund
description:
Karateka is a martial arts action-adventure game developed and published by Broderbund in 1984. Players assume the role of a skilled martial artist on a quest to rescue a princess from an evil warlord's fortress. With its fluid animation and intuitive controls, Karateka offers a unique blend of combat and platforming gameplay.

            The game features a series of challenging levels, where players must defeat enemies using various martial arts techniques while avoiding traps and obstacles. With its cinematic presentation and compelling storyline, Karateka captivated players with its immersive gameplay and memorable characters, earning it a place as a classic in the history of video games.

title: Raid on Bungeling Bay
label: Brøderbund
description:
Raid on Bungeling Bay was designed and programmed by Will Wright for the Commodore 64 and first published by Brøderbund in 1984. Ariolasoft published the UK release. It was Wright's first commercial game, several years before he created SimCity.

The player pilots a helicopter from an aircraft carrier and must find and destroy six factories spread across the islands of Bungeling Bay. The factories do not simply wait to be attacked: they produce and strengthen enemy defences, escalating from gun emplacements and fighters to guided missiles and a battleship. Returning to the carrier allows the helicopter to rearm and repair, provided the carrier itself survives.

Its scrolling world and increasingly organised opposition made it more strategic than a conventional shoot-'em-up. Wright's experience building and observing the simulated island environment became an important step towards the ideas he later developed in SimCity.
sources: Sources reviewed: original game instructions; MobyGames release record; Will Wright game-history accounts.

title: The Castles of Dr. Creep
label: Brøderbund
description:
The Castles of Dr. Creep is a Commodore 64 puzzle-platform game written by Ed Hobbs and first published by Brøderbund in 1984. Ariolasoft published the UK edition in 1985.

Players explore a collection of large, interconnected castles and must solve each one before escaping. Rooms contain switches, ladders, moving walkways, lifts, trapdoors, force fields and teleporters, alongside hazards drawn from classic horror films: mummies, vampires, Frankenstein's monster and other residents of Dr. Creep's estate.

The game includes thirteen main castles plus a tutorial and can be played alone or cooperatively by two players. Progress depends less on quick reactions than on understanding how rooms connect and how one mechanism affects another, making it an unusually elaborate mixture of platform action and environmental puzzle solving for its period.
sources: Sources reviewed: original UK manual; MobyGames release record; contemporary and official re-release descriptions.

title: Marble Madness
label: Electronic Arts
description:
Marble Madness is the home-computer adaptation of Atari Games' influential 1984 arcade game. Players race a marble through six isometric obstacle courses against a strict time limit, contending with ramps, narrow ledges, moving hazards and hostile marbles.

Electronic Arts published the home versions, with Ariolasoft handling European editions. The surviving Ariolasoft material includes Commodore 64 packaging and an Amiga disk, alongside versions for Apple II and IBM PC compatibles.

title: Movie Maker
label: Electronic Arts
description:
Movie Maker is an animation construction program developed by Interactive Picture Systems. It lets users draw characters and shapes, assemble them into sequences, add sound effects and play the finished animation at different speeds. Completed movies can be saved as self-playing files that do not require the authoring program.

Originally released for Atari 8-bit computers in 1984, Movie Maker was republished by Electronic Arts in 1985 and appeared on Commodore 64 and Apple II as well. The surviving Apple II packshot confirms Ariolasoft's European edition.
sources: Ariolasoft Apple II packaging; Centre for Computing History collection record; contemporary Electronic Arts and Interactive Picture Systems records.

title: Stealth
developer: Tracy LaGrone and Richard E. Sansom
label: Brøderbund
description:
Stealth is a pseudo-3D rail shooter designed by Tracy LaGrone and Richard E. Sansom and published by Brøderbund in 1984. At the controls of a low-flying Stealth Starfighter, the player must penetrate hostile territory and destroy the Dark Tower, stronghold of the Council of Nine.

Warp-fighters attack from the air while radar towers, photon tanks, missiles and laser artillery defend the landscape below. Positive energy fields replenish the ship, while negative fields drain it. Ariolasoft released Stealth in Europe for Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit computers.
sources: Ariolasoft Autumn/Winter 1985 catalogue; original Ariolasoft Commodore 64 packaging; Brøderbund release records.

title: Degas
label: Ariolasoft
description:
DEGAS — the Design & Entertainment Graphic Arts System — was a bitmap painting program created by Tom Hudson for the Atari ST and published by Batteries Included in 1985. Its working title had been HUDraw before Hudson adopted the name inspired by the French artist Edgar Degas.

One of the first full-featured art packages for the new Atari ST, DEGAS supported all three of the machine's display modes and supplied tools for freehand drawing, shapes, fills, text and detailed pixel editing. Its PI1, PI2 and PI3 picture formats became widely recognised across the ST software scene.

Ariolasoft published DEGAS in the UK and Europe. It was an Atari ST-exclusive application.
sources: Sources reviewed: contemporary Atari ST buyer's guides; Tom Hudson development history; platform and release records.

title: Bug Blitz
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Bug Blitz is a multi-directional Commodore 64 shooter created by András Pohl of Andromeda Software and published by Ariolasoft in 1985. The player pilots a spacecraft through dangerous tunnels to reach caverns occupied by an army of mutant bugs.

After destroying the bugs in a cavern, the ship must retrace its route to the planet's surface. Even there it is not safe: randomly pulsing energy fields cover the landscape and can destroy the ship before the mission is complete.

title: Print Master
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Print Master is a creative graphics program from Unison World that lets users design and print personalised greetings cards, signs, stationery, calendars, banners and memos without programming or drawing skills. Designs are assembled from menus of borders, graphics, layouts and fonts before adding a message and sending the result to a printer.

The Ariolasoft catalogue advertised Commodore 64 and IBM PC editions, with more than 100 prepared graphics, eleven patterns, eight fonts and eleven border designs. The surviving Ariolasoft packshot is for the Atari 520 ST edition.
sources: Ariolasoft Autumn/Winter 1985 catalogue; surviving Ariolasoft Atari ST packaging; Unison World Print Master records.

title: Saucer Attack
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Saucer Attack is James D. Sachs' Commodore 64 shoot-'em-up, released in Europe by Ariolasoft. Alien saucers are attacking Washington, D.C., and the player must destroy them with carefully aimed energy balls. Every missed shot scores for the invaders, so accuracy is essential.

The pace quickens as the battle continues. Score enough points and the player earns a chance to attack the mothership and save the city. The original Ariolasoft packaging promoted the game's high-resolution graphics and rich sound effects.
sources: Original Ariolasoft front and back packaging; Ariolasoft Autumn/Winter 1985 catalogue; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saucer_Attack!

title: Paperclip
label: Ariolasoft
description:
PaperClip was the flagship word processor from Canadian software company Batteries Included. The Commodore 64 version was written by Steve Douglas; Steve Ahlstrom and Dan Moore produced the substantially different Atari 8-bit version, drawing on the editor from the Action! programming language.

PaperClip combined document editing and printing with unusually capable features for an 8-bit home computer, including macros, multiple editing windows, search and replace, block operations and mail-merge facilities. It became one of the best-known serious applications for both platforms.

Ariolasoft published PaperClip in the UK in 1985 for the Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit family. Both Ariolasoft editions were supplied on disk; there were no cassette editions.
sources: Sources reviewed: contemporary Antic coverage; Batteries Included company history; platform and authorship records. Ariolasoft format detail supplied from first-hand company recollection.

title: Mail Order Monsters
developer: Paul Reiche III, Evan Robinson and Nicky Robinson
label: Electronic Arts
description:
Mail Order Monsters is an action-strategy game created by Paul Reiche III, Evan Robinson and Nicky Robinson. Electronic Arts published the Commodore 64 edition in 1985 and the Atari 8-bit version followed in 1986; Ariolasoft published the game in Europe.

Players create and customise creatures, buying weapons and unusual abilities before sending them into battle. The game supports head-to-head combat, capture the flag and a single-player contest against computer-controlled opponents. Terrain affects the fighting, while successful monsters can be saved to disk and improved through later victories.

Its mixture of creature customisation, persistent combatants and competitive action has since been recognised as an early forerunner of later monster-battling games.

title: Degas Elite
label: Ariolasoft
description:
DEGAS Elite was Tom Hudson's expanded successor to DEGAS, published by Batteries Included in 1986 for the Atari ST. It retained compatibility with pictures created in the original program while considerably enlarging its creative toolset.

Elite added multiple work screens, clip-art handling and advanced block operations including scaling, rotation, skewing and distortion. Its colour-cycling animation controls let artists set the direction and speed of palette changes, producing animated effects without redrawing the image frame by frame.

Ariolasoft published DEGAS Elite in the UK and Europe. Like its predecessor, it was exclusive to the Atari ST.
sources: Sources reviewed: contemporary Atari ST buyer's guides and magazine coverage; Tom Hudson development history; platform and release records.

title: Sepulcri
label: Ariolasoft
description:
Sepulcri is a 1986 Amstrad CPC platform game programmed by Chris Sawyer and published by Ariolasoft. It was adapted from Sawyer's earlier Memotech MTX game Sepulcri Scelerati, published by Megastar Games in 1985. When Sawyer subsequently offered the game to Ariolasoft for the Amstrad CPC, Ariolasoft shortened the title and commissioned replacement graphics from Jill Lawson at 4am Designs. This Ariolasoft edition was released only for the CPC; the Memotech MTX should not be confused with the unrelated MSX standard.

In the year 2075, engineers testing the first Strategic Defence Initiative satellite send a tiny robot inside its main computer to inspect the circuitry and report its many faults. Unfortunately, one confused technician has miniaturised male sheep and installed them in place of conventional RAM, leaving the robot to contend with some unusually literal computer hazards.

The first task is to explore the rooms and activate all 50 dip-switches by jumping on them. Moving enemies, sharp surfaces, unstable integrated circuits and floating points threaten the robot along the way. Once every switch has been found, the robot must enter ROTTES - Ridiculously Over The Top Exit Security - and alter ten code posts to spell LETMEOUTOK before locating the exit.

The original Ariolasoft instructions credit Chris Sawyer with programming, Jill Lawson at 4am Designs with graphics and puns, the Tech Team with the implausible storyline, and IFRIT with the instructions. They also document redefinable controls, a pause function and an unusually useful screen-dump feature intended to help players map the game's rooms.
sources: Memotech MTX software records for Sepulcri Scelerati (Megastar Games, 1985); first-hand Ariolasoft production recollection; original Sepulcri instruction booklet, Ariolasoft UK Ltd (1986), page 2: 'Programmed by Chris Sawyer' and 'Graphics and Puns by Jill Lawson at 4am Designs'.

title: Werewolves of London
label: Ariolasoft
description:
The cancelled 1987 launch

Viz Design had previously worked with Ariolasoft on Bride of Frankenstein. Werewolves of London was heavily previewed in 1987 as a major forthcoming full-price release for Ariolasoft's Viz Design label.

The Amstrad CPC edition did reach production in 1987, and surviving original Ariolasoft retail copies show that a small number made it into circulation. Ariolasoft UK ceased trading around the time of the intended launch, however, preventing the planned wider release.

The title was subsequently picked up by Mastertronic and received its widespread commercial release in 1989 as a £1.99 budget game.

Verified original Ariolasoft format: Amstrad CPC.
sources: Sources reviewed: The Games Machine issue 2, page 75 (https://archive.org/details/the-games-machine-02/page/n74/mode/1up); contemporary 1987 magazine previews and reviews; MobyGames release records; World of Spectrum; Lemon64; CPC-Power.

title: Challenge of the Gobots
label: Reaktor
description:
Challenge of the Gobots is a 1987 arcade action game published on the Reaktor label. Game design and coding are credited in the original instructions to Tony Crowther and Ross Goodley, with storyline by RATT, text by K. Blake and R. Goodley, audio by We M.U.S.I.C., and the instructions by IFRIT.

The player takes the role of the courageous Leader 1. Scooter clones are collected by landing on them, then released with the bomb control and hurled at enemy bases. Huge rocks can also be torn from the ground or ceiling and thrown at enemies, although they cannot damage the bases. Destroying the bases advances the player through the levels, while aggressive play fills the score bar and can earn promotion or an extra life.

The instructions also describe rescuing humans who fall from the copter, a task reserved for players who have reached the top rank, plus configurable controls, a high-score display, and a practice level before beginning the main game.
sources: Preserved original Challenge of the Gobots multilingual instructions; OCR and visual review.

title: Out of this World
label: Reaktor
description: Out of This World is a colourful side-scrolling shoot-'em-up designed by Bettertech, the company run by James Poole and Gary Yorke, and published by Ariolasoft under the Reaktör label in 1987 for the Commodore 64, Amstrad CPC and ZX Spectrum. Eight looping worlds combine enemy waves, collectable weapon pods and enormous end-of-world Guardians. A playable browser restoration preserves the Spectrum loading screen, reconstructed CPC artwork and Jason C. Brooke's original C64 SID music.

title: Starfox
label: Reaktor
description:
Starfox is a space-combat game developed by Realtime Games and published on Ariolasoft's Reaktor label in 1987. Its story is set in 2746, after centuries of conflict have left the eight planets of the Hyturian system locked in full-scale war. The long-standing Rubicon barrier has been breached, and the player is sent to discover how and restore the peace.

The surviving multilingual packaging covers the Commodore 64, Amstrad CPC and ZX Spectrum editions. It credits James Poole as producer, Harry Oversoft as director, Alex and Servo with first art-unit direction, Wong with financial direction, and Mandy and Jules with press and co-ordination.
sources: Original Ariolasoft/Reaktor packaging; first-hand production recollection supplied by James Poole.

title: Ziggurat
label: Reaktor
description:
Ziggurat is a 1988 isometric arcade adventure developed by Tigress Designs and presented by Ariolasoft's Reaktor label. The preserved title screen provides direct contemporary credit for the production: the game was written by Chris Sawyer, designed by Tigress Designs, and features graphics by ALK.

Players explore a maze-like structure on a treasure hunt, navigating interconnected rooms while avoiding their inhabitants and making use of a selectable inventory. The controls include jumping, firing, laying a lure, reversing direction and manipulating objects. Contemporary coverage advised players to draw a map as they explored.

The surviving credit screen is particularly valuable because it distinguishes Tigress Designs' design role from Sawyer's programming credit, explicitly displaying the words 'Written by Chris Sawyer'.
sources: Original Ziggurat title and credit screen preserved by CPCWiki: 'Written by Chris Sawyer'; CPCRulez preservation record and contemporary ASM review transcription.
